blocks.x: Applying Cyber & Zero-Trust to Semiconductors & Hardware: the context that decides the design, the weekly cadence, the towers involved, and committed outcomes per gate.

Hardware companies run the longest R&D loops under the sharpest IP threats: design simulation, fab yield (their own or partners'), supply-chain visibility and product security. Compute acceleration and governed data are the compounding assets.

items: Design data state-grade interest; exfiltration paths open.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Compliance, Audit & Digital Trust, Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation, Threat Intelligence & Managed SOC from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Design/simulation, Supply-chain visibility, Yield analytics) on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass. Governance inherits the sector frame — Export controls among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Secure at the control plane: posture, workload and data security engineered into the platform.
Secure the models themselves: prompt-injection defense, agent containment and AI red-teaming.
Assume breach, plan recovery: resilience engineered, rehearsed and measured.

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Technology & SaaS level this capability reads as: continuous SOC 2/ISO evidence with framework-unified register (audit prep down 60-80%). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

This capability runs on the cadence set out below; the rhythm is fixed, the scope is signed. Weeks 1–2 belong to measurement: the baseline metric is captured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 run a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — steered by a control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 convert the pilot into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, and close with a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses a gate is stopped or redirected on the record.
